options: Moving the computation close to where the data resides on the storage or data node, instead of moving large data to the computation
Knowing the geographical location from which data was generated
Storing data in the country where it was generated to satisfy sovereignty laws
Copying all data from data nodes into the master nodes before querying
Separating compute and storage into different clusters
questions.explanation: Data Locality is the process of moving the computation close to where the actual data resides on the storage/data node, rather than moving large data to the computation.

questions.stem: Traditionally, where was data fetched to for computation in analysis?
options: From master nodes into storage nodes
From storage or data nodes into master nodes
From the cloud into on-premises servers
From a Data Room into a Data Lake
From columnar storage into row storage
questions.explanation: Traditionally, to use data for analysis, the data was fetched at the backend from storage/data nodes into master nodes for computation.

questions.stem: Why did fetching data into master nodes for computation become impractical?
options: Because master nodes cannot run SQL
Because network links between nodes were removed
Because semi-structured and unstructured data now runs to terabytes and petabytes on clusters of hundreds of data nodes, while master nodes are normally few
Because data must stay in the country where it was generated
Because master nodes only store metadata
questions.explanation: Semi-structured and unstructured data brings huge storage requirements, in TB and even PB, hosted on clusters of hundreds of storage/data nodes. Pulling that much data into the few master nodes for computation is not possible.

questions.stem: With the introduction of Big Data, Hadoop and HDFS, in what shape is data stored on the data nodes?
options: As documents
As key-value pairs
As graph nodes and edges
As blocks
As spreadsheets
questions.explanation: With Big Data, Hadoop and HDFS, data is stored in the shape of blocks, and the Data Locality concept surfaced of taking the query to the storage/data nodes.

questions.stem: Under Data Locality, what is sent back from the storage or data nodes after the query is processed there?
options: The complete raw dataset
Every block that the query touched
A copy of the whole cluster's metadata
The query itself, for re-execution on the master node
Only the processed data
questions.explanation: Instead of fetching data for computation, the query is taken to the storage/data nodes, processed there, and only the processed data is fetched back.

questions.stem: In a nutshell, when is a query said to exhibit Data Locality?
options: When the query runs on the same node where the data is located
When the query is written in standard SQL
When the query returns results in real time
When the query is executed on a master node
When the query uses columnar rather than row storage
questions.explanation: In a nutshell, when a query runs on the same node where the data is located, it is called Data Locality.

questions.stem: Which newer concept is described as surfacing in recent times, in contrast to Data Locality?
options: Pulling whole datasets into master nodes
Separating computing and storage
Storing all data in a single Physical Data Room
Replacing HDFS with operating-system file systems
Merging master nodes and data nodes into one
questions.explanation: In recent times, a new concept of separating computing and storage has been surfacing.

questions.stem: How relevant is the literal reading of Data Locality as simply knowing the location of the data?
options: Entirely accurate: that is the whole meaning
Entirely wrong: location has nothing to do with it
Partially relevant: the name suggests location, but the concept is about moving computation to the data
Relevant only for relational databases
Relevant only for cloud storage
questions.explanation: As the name suggests, Data Locality looks like knowing the location of the data, which is only partially relevant. The concept is about processing queries where the data is residing.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT part of the history of how data was pulled for processing before Data Locality?
options: Initially the whole data was pulled
Later, blocks were pulled
Later, the columnar pull concept came in
Later, data was pulled as printed reports
Eventually the query was taken to the data instead
questions.explanation: The history runs from pulling the whole data, to pulling blocks, to the columnar pull concept, and finally to taking the query to the data nodes. Printed reports are not part of it.

questions.stem: What was the critical requirement that led to the Data Locality concept?
options: To encrypt data on every data node
To reduce the number of master nodes to one
To convert all data to structured form
To keep data in the country where it was generated
To process queries where the data is residing
questions.explanation: It was a critical requirement to process queries where the data is residing, because pulling terabytes or petabytes into a few master nodes was not possible.
